question: Prepare a Q3 2025 bank-disclosure brief for a PE portfolio CFO. Compare JPMorgan and Bank of America on CET1 ratio, estimated uninsured deposits, and third-quarter net interest income. State the reporting period and units, cite each figure, and flag disclosures that are not comparable.

summary.text: At September 30, 2025 JPMorgan reported a Standardized CET1 capital ratio of 14.8% and third-quarter net interest income of $23,966 million, with firmwide estimated uninsured deposits of $1,548.1 billion.
Bank of America reported a Standardized CET1 capital ratio of 11.6% at September 30, 2025 against a 10.7% minimum requirement, and third-quarter net interest income of $15,233 million.

BAC's only uninsured-deposit disclosure in the excerpts is as of December 31, 2024 ($646.2 billion U.S. and $124.9 billion non-U.S.), so it is not date-comparable with JPM's September 30, 2025 figure.
BAC's reported net interest income includes an FTE adjustment of $154 million for the third quarter of 2025, a basis difference to note when comparing NII levels.

claims.text: JPMorgan's Standardized CET1 capital ratio was 14.8% at September 30, 2025 (vs. a 12.3% Standardized requirement).
JPMorgan's net interest income was $23,966 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, up 2% from $23,405 million a year earlier.
JPMorgan's firmwide estimated uninsured deposits were $1,548.1 billion at September 30, 2025 (and $1,414.0 billion at December 31, 2024).
claims.quote: At September 30, 2025 and December 31, 2024, Firmwide estimated uninsured deposits were $1,548.1 billion and $1,414.0 billion, respectively, primarily reflecting wholesale operating deposits.

claims.text: Bank of America's CET1 capital ratio under the Standardized approach was 11.6 percent at September 30, 2025, above its 10.7 percent minimum requirement.
